title: GCP Pub/Sub: `subscriptionSize` is removed — the scaler refuses the trigger

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **GCP PubSub Scaler**: The `subscriptionSize` setting is DEPRECATED and is removed in v2.20 - Use `mode` and `value` instead (#7720)
remediation: The tag flips to `deprecated=` at v2.20.0 and the parser rejects a trigger that still sets `subscriptionSize` — every gcp-pubsub trigger named stops scaling after the hop. Replace it with `mode: SubscriptionSize` + `value` before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "gcp-pubsub") and (.metadata // {} | has("subscriptionSize"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row is refused by the 2.20 scaler

title: Azure Data Explorer: `clientSecretFromEnv` support is removed — the secret must come from a TriggerAuthentication

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **Azure Data Explorer Scaler**: Remove clientSecretFromEnv support (#7554)
remediation: Filed by upstream under Fixes, not Breaking Changes. pkg/scalers/azure_data_explorer_scaler.go at v2.20.0 declares `clientSecret` with `order=authParams` only, so `clientSecretFromEnv` on each azure-data-explorer trigger named is no longer resolved and the scaler fails with "clientSecret was not found in metadata" after the hop. Move the secret to a TriggerAuthentication `secretTargetRef` (`clientSecret`) or use `podIdentity` before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "azure-data-explorer") and (.metadata // {} | has("clientSecretFromEnv"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row stops authenticating on the hop

title: ArangoDB, Loki, Prometheus and PredictKube: the unused `authModes` trigger-metadata key is dropped

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **General**: Remove dead code from authentication package and drop unused `authModes` field from ArangoDB, Loki, Prometheus and PredictKube scalers (#7726)
remediation: `authModes` is read from the TriggerAuthentication (`authParams`), never from trigger metadata; 2.20 deletes the dead metadata field. Each trigger named carries the key where it was always ignored — remove it and keep `authModes` on the TriggerAuthentication.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "arangodb" or .type == "loki" or .type == "prometheus" or .type == "predictkube") and (.metadata // {} | has("authModes"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row carries authModes in trigger metadata, where it is ignored

title: Cron trigger: metric names for comma-separated cron expressions change

detection.reason: the cron expression values (start/end) are not projected — only the key names are

quote: **Cron Scaler**: Fix metric name generation so cron expressions with comma-separated values no longer produce invalid metric names (#7448)
remediation: A cron trigger whose `start` or `end` expression contains a comma produced an invalid HPA metric name before 2.20; the name is now normalised, so dashboards or alerts keyed on the old metric name for the cron triggers named must be updated. Scaling itself is unaffected.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select(.type == "cron") | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row is a cron trigger; one whose start/end contains a comma gets a new metric name on the hop

title: ScaledObject status: HPA health moves from the `Ready` condition to a new `HPAActive` condition

detection.reason: which condition an alert, GitOps health check or script reads is not in the collected projection

quote: **General**: Introduce a dedicated `HPAActive` condition on `ScaledObject` mirroring the HPA's own `ScalingActive` status, so transient HPA metric gaps no longer flip the `Ready` condition to `False` (#7914)
remediation: From 2.20.2 a transient HPA metric gap no longer flips `Ready` to False; it is reported on the new `HPAActive` condition (mirroring the HPA's `ScalingActive`). Anything that watched `Ready` to catch metric outages — alerts, Argo CD health checks, scripts — must read `HPAActive` as well; anything that paged on `Ready` flapping stops paging.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) Ready=\((.status.conditions // [])[] | select(.type == "Ready") | .status) HPAActive=\((.status.conditions // [])[] | select(.type == "HPAActive") | .status)"'  # after the hop every row carries HPAActive; before it the column is empty

title: Temporal: `buildId`, `selectAllActive` and `selectUnversioned` are announced for removal in 2.21

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: name=buildId, order=triggerMetadata;resolvedEnv, optional, deprecatedAnnounce=The 'buildId' setting is DEPRECATED and will be removed in v2.21 because Temporal Server is dropping support for the Rules-Based Versioning APIs - Use 'workerDeploymentName' and 'workerDeploymentBuildId' instead
remediation: Temporal Server is dropping the Rules-Based Versioning APIs. On each temporal trigger named, remove the three settings for unversioned workers, or move versioned workers to `workerDeploymentName` + `workerDeploymentBuildId`. 2.20 logs a KEDAScalerInfo event; 2.21 refuses the trigger.

title: Admission webhook rejects a ScaledObject whose derived HPA name `keda-hpa-<name>` exceeds 63 characters

detection.reason: the name filter runs over every ScaledObject in the snapshot; one that sets a custom HPA name is listed too and needs no change

quote: HPA name %q derived from scaledobject is %d characters long; must be no more than %d characters; set spec.advanced.horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig.name to a shorter name or shorten the scaledobject name
remediation: Each ScaledObject named is 55+ characters long, so its default HPA name `keda-hpa-<name>` breaks the 63-character DNS label limit and the 2.20 webhook rejects the object on its next update. Set `spec.advanced.horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig.name` to a shorter name (an object that already sets one is unaffected) or rename the ScaledObject.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.advanced.horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig.name == null and (.metadata.name | test("^.{55,}$"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) (\(.metadata.name | length) chars)"'  # each row is rejected by the 2.20 webhook on its next update

title: Admission webhook rejects a ScaledObject whose name exceeds 63 characters (used as a label value)
quote: scaledobject name %q is %d characters long; must be no more than %d characters because it is used as the %q label value
remediation: KEDA labels the ScaledObject and its HPA with `scaledobject.keda.sh/name=<name>`, and a label value is capped at 63 characters. Each ScaledObject named is longer and is rejected by the 2.20 webhook on its next update — recreate it under a shorter name.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^.{64,}$")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) (\(.metadata.name | length) chars)"'  # each row is rejected by the 2.20 webhook on its next update
coversNotes: General: Reject ScaledObject creation and update when the name exceeds 63 characters…

title: Admission webhook rejects `podIdentity.externalId` without `roleArn`

detection.reason: the rejection pairs externalId with roleArn; the projection records each as set, not the pairing

quote: externalID of PodIdentity requires roleArn to be set
remediation: An AWS `externalId` is only meaningful on an assumed role. Each TriggerAuthentication named sets `spec.podIdentity.externalId` and is rejected by the 2.20 webhook on its next update unless `roleArn` is set too.
verifyCommand: kubectl get triggerauthentications.keda.sh,clustertriggerauthentications.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.podIdentity.externalId != null and .spec.podIdentity.roleArn == null) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is rejected by the 2.20 webhook on its next update
